hints: The normal to a circle at any point passes through the centre $(-1, 3)$.
walkthrough:
The normal is the straight line through the centre and contact point.
The normal to the circle at $Q(2, 7)$ is the line connecting centre $(-1, 3)$ and $Q$:
$$m_{\text{norm}} = \dfrac{7 - 3}{2 - (-1)} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$

Write the normal equation in slope-intercept form:
$$y - 3 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x + 1) \implies y = \dfrac{4}{3}x + \dfrac{4}{3} + 3 = \dfrac{4}{3}x + \dfrac{13}{3}$$
